channel.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "SCP - The Infinite Quarter" - A simple 25¢ coin that can multiply

item.title: Re: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Ok these are fair points I didn’t really consider when first designing this concept. I had considered making all the coins anomalous but by doing so i felt it would just be constant foundation having to deal with multiple anomalous coins duplicating and that would of been too messy.

I’ll go back to the drawing board and try to remake it

item.title: Re: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
several change machines would be purchased by the foundations and placed in various laundry mats and arcades where agents disguised as workers will place the half the non anomalous coins in the change machines and gather the money for funding

I'm…not sure I follow this? Is the plan 'the foundation owns a bunch of change machines and uses them to convert the coins into notes' because uh,,,that's not how money works

Beyond this, my core issue is that 'the foundation tries to work out which coin is anomalous' feels…like it'd be really uninteresting as a follow up to the description since we already know that it's just, one coin being anomalous; but it also feels like the actual investigation might be just, really boring and a lot of repetitive 'we tested coins 1 through 100, none are anomalous' kinda things.

I feel like this needs a stronger central narrative that actually focusses on the like, coin duplicating and the Foundation using this for their benefit, and like, that going somewhere, whether it's like…just the Foundation gradually like destabilising the economy by printing money or like, the treasury department investigating them and trying to arrest folk for creating counterfeit currency or something.

item.title: Re: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Building off what AnActualCrow said, my concern with your central narrative section is that it doesn't really…do anything? There's this kinda, little mystery but there's not really a lot of time spent developing it and also bear in mind: this is a SCP article. Your addenda/discovery section exploring the mystery is going to come after the Description of what the SCP is, and so the reader will already know that the answer to the question 'where did the man get all the coins from' is 'infinite quarter'.

The idea of the Foundation using this for funding is interesting and building off that so it goes somewhere could be really fun: it might be worth considering like, how this could break something or draw unwanted attention that causes conflict.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It looks like you're trying to set up a mystery in your central narrative (how did this man get all these quarters?) but the answer to the mystery isn't particularly interesting (an anomaly that makes quarters out of nothing).

Compare your mystery to something like SCP-5005 (spoilers ahead BTW). One of the mysteries 5005 sets up is "where did this giant magic lamp come from?" and the answer is "it's the lure of a massive anglerfish". Once you know the answer, the complete situation "this town exists in a sea of nothingness because of the light of a giant dead anglerfish's lure" is a lot more interesting than "this guy has a lot of quarters because he has an SCP that makes quarters".

The simplest solution would be changing your anomaly so that there's some deeper implication to making all those quarters. Say, for example, that the anomaly is a machine that grinds cute baby animals into a pulp and then turns them into quarters. Now, your complete situation isn't just "this guy has a lot of quarters because he has an SCP that makes quarters"— it's "this guy has a lot of quarters because he was willing to grind up tons of cute baby animals for money."

item.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Ok so I made some edits of this scp concept to make it more interesting. If you wanna know what the actual changes are look at my most recent reply

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Infinite Quarter” is a 2019 San Antonio Mission Texas Quarter with the head side of the coin scratched up by unknown means. The quarter seems like an average coin but when left unobserved the coin will start to rapidly multiply until observed or all open space is occupied. All other instances of the scp do not share the same anomalous duplication ability as the main coin and will only share the ability of ceasing duplication when the coins are observed though if one were to observe a duplicated instance of the coin and not the original coin it will not stop the original from duplicating.

Central Narrative: The coin would of first been discovered when foundation agents saw news of a vending machine worker being severely injured after what eye witness described as an avalanche of quarters bursting out of a vending machine when they opened it. They took app the quarters and the machine to determine which item was the anomalous item as well as giving all witnesses amnestics. After finding the anomalous coin they brought it to the foundation and contain it in a specially made plastic case big enough to fit a single quarter.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: All duplicated instances of the coin will be in perfect condition and not sharing any of the scratch marks on the head side of the coin like the original does. It would also be that the coin itself doesn’t just create more of itself out of thin air but instead breaks up most materials and converting it in an unknown manner into duplicate coins to the point all the space is filled. I had also thought to make it so that the actual original coin is always the easiest to spot as to make it more easier to be observed to warrant its duplication stopping when viewed.

Additional notes: possible idea is the scp foundation will sometimes use this scp for possible funding for resources and the like but in order to prevent unwanted attention, several change machines would be purchased by the foundations and placed in various laundry mats and arcades where agents disguised as workers will place the half the non anomalous coins in the change machines and gather the money for funding with the other half being melted down to help keep things under control
